The proposed method uses a Support Vector Machine (SVM) to ensure that the gradients recovered from Bayer pattern pictures are robust enough to be employed in pedestrian detection algorithms based on Histograms of Oriented Gradients (HOG). Benchmark datasets from MIT, Caltech, and INRIA were used to test the proposed technique. In comparison to other previous techniques, it is inferred that our proposed technique outperforms them by maintaining good accuracy.

articleTitle: A Improved Training Method for Deep Learning Based Anatomical Classification of X-Rays
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Every day, numerous medical images are sent to hospitals and tele-radiology facilities. These comprise a variety of techniques and body parts, such as elbow X-rays, head CT scans, and chest MRIs. These should be given to radiologists who are knowledgeable about the particular anatomy and modality. However, sometimes the scan's technicians enter the incorrect anatomy, employ a different naming scheme, or enter no information at all. There is a need for a vision-based anatomy classification system that can be applied in the absence or corruption of image-related meta-data. Before allocating a case to a radiologist, a manual screen may correctly estimate the anatomy from an X-Ray image. Our proposed solution will provide an automatic anatomy classification with improved training method using deep neural networks. We set out to develop a pre-trained supervised deep learning model that examines X-rays and returns the X-ray's anatomy from a preset set of anatomies in order to solve the given challenge. Here, we also suggest an improved training method to increase classification accuracy. With our present approach, we could accurately map reports and obtain anatomical classification accuracy of more than 95% using X-ray clinical data.

articleTitle: Transformer-based Models for Language Identification: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Language Identification (LI) is a crucial task in natural language processing (NLP) with significant implications for various NLP applications, including machine translation, sentiment analysis, and text summarization. In this paper, we present a novel LI approach that harnesses the power of transformers, which are state-of-the-art models in NLP. We conduct a comprehensive comparative study between the DistilBERT model, ALBERT model and the XLM-RoBERTa model for LI. Our findings reveal that the DistilBERT model, with its lightweight design, offers comparable accuracy with reduced computational requirements. ALBERT model is designed to achieve parameter reduction by employing parameter-sharing techniques and factorized embedding parameterization. Further-more, we observe that XLM-RoBERTa, a multilingual variant of RoBERTa, surpasses both ALBERT and DistilBERT in handling diverse LI tasks.

articleTitle: Prevention of Road Accidents Through Smart Assistive Technology with Artificial Intelligence Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: The creation of a sophisticated two-wheeler helmet in India seeks to drastically lower the amount of traffic accidents brought on by careless and inebriated driving. It is critical to solve this issue since, according to data, two-wheelers are involved in around 25% of traffic incidents in India. Enormous number of sensors have been incorporated into the construction of the smart helmet. First of all, alcohol sensors are built in to determine whether a cyclist has drunk before riding. This function can serve as a preventative measure by discouraging people from driving when intoxicated, hence lowering the possibility of accidents brought on by poor judgment. Additionally, a rider's helmet is continually monitored by an infrared sensor. Additionally, the helmet has a vibration detector attached to detect harsh impacts during accidents. This sensor will send an alarm to emergency services or predetermined contacts in the case of a collision, enabling prompt aid and potentially life-saving treatments. The two-wheeler's whereabouts may be tracked in real-time thanks to the GPS capability. The GPS on the helmet can determine the rider's location in the event of an accident, assisting first responders in quickly reaching the scene even in outlying or unfamiliar locations. The ingenious helmet attempts to make two-wheeler riders in India safer by integrating these cutting-edge sensors. The entire system can provide fast aid in times of need in addition to preventing accidents brought on by intoxicated, careless, or fatigued driving. This program might potentially save many lives and encourage safe driving habits, which would ultimately lead to a decline in traffic accidents and their severe effects.

articleTitle: AI-Based Autonomous Paddy Farm using Smart and Precise Irrigation System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: With the rampant growth of the global population and the increasing need for agricultural products, farmers confront a critical hurdle of ensuring an adequate supply of water resources for irrigation to meet these escalating demands. Amid limited water resources, farmers must embrace innovative solutions and efficient water management practices in the era of Agriculture 4.0 turning this concept into a tangible reality to meet the growing demand for efficient farming practices. By integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) to gather and analyze agricultural data, we now have the capability to make more accurate and informed decisions in agriculture. In this, an innovative and adaptable irrigation system is introduced which prioritizes efficiency and cost-effectiveness by minimizing resource consumption. This strategy leverages the capabilities of Machine Learning (ML) algorithms to elevate the level of agricultural intelligence. By employing a suite of sensors, including those for soil moisture, temperature, and rainfall, within an environment conducive to prolonged plant growth, the collected data to construct SVM models findings indicate that SVM outperforms other models (LR, NN, NB) with an impressive recognition rate of 98.5% and a minimal root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.10. Through this system, crop irrigation is achieved with a high level of precision, entirely automated, and without the need for human intervention. As a result, this technology leads to a substantial reduction in water consumption, up to 50%.

articleTitle: Cardiac Arrhythmia - Prediction and Classification using Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Untreated, arrhythmia is a potentially life-threatening condition that can lead to severe illness in patients. Early detection of heart arrhythmias can save lives. Based on ECG recordings. New advances in various types of equipment and machine learning models provide an opportunity to use computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) to make ECG classification procedures applicable in a real clinical setting. This allows classification of electrocardiographic arrhythmias between patients. The objective of this paper is to design and evaluate an innovative cross-patient approach for analyzing extensive electrocardiogram datasets, with the goal of enhancing the identification of rare arrhythmia We study four supervised machine learning models: support vector machine (SVM), k-nearest neighbor (KNN), random forest (RF), and a suite of three methods. We will test the effectiveness of these strategies in classifying: normal beaters (NOR), left leg blockers (LBBB), right leg blockers (RBBB), failure of atrial complexes (PAC) and premature ventricular complexes (PVC), next. segmenting and normalizing the data, obtaining patients' actual ECG data from MIT-DB, and measuring four parameters: precision, accuracy, recall, and f1 score. The results of the experiment show that, without the use of complex data preprocessing or engineering methods, the SVM classifier outperforms other methods using our patient interviews in all cases. An achieved Calculation value accuracy is of 0.84; is still very important. ECG is important in using the arrhythmia classification model. This approach is more accurate in clinical settings. where multiple ECG signals are collected from different patients.

articleTitle: A Cost-Effective Navigational Aid for the visually impaired
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Even though technology is improving at an amazing rate, there is still no product on the market that is easy for blind or visually impaired people to use and doesn't cost too much. People who are blind or visually impaired find it hard to do everyday things. If the navigational aid device is linked to the foldable tick, it may help blind or visually impaired people get around and make their job easier. The final product will already have sensors built right in. With these devices, the product will be able to find any nearby objects or people who are trying to get in. Someone will feel a vibration and get a reaction from the device right away if an object or obstacle comes within range of the ultrasonic sensor. This will teach the person in question a lesson. Since the system is small, it is easy to move and set up whenever it is needed. In order to reach this goal, the gadget was designed with a feature that lets the lines roll up when they're not in use. The person who uses the stick will never have any trouble folding it because of this built-in feature. At the very bottom of this thing is a swivel wheel that can be attached to it and turned in any direction—all the way around. Because of the extra benefit, the user doesn't have to lift the stick and tap it on the ground to see what the environment ahead him looks like. Because of this, the amount of work that needs to be done to finish this task is directly decreased. The main goal of this work is to make a blind stick that is both useful and relatively cheap.

articleTitle: An IoT-based Home Automation System using NodeMCU and Blynk IoT App
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has revolutionized the way of living by connecting everyday devices to the Internet. One of the most promising applications of IoT is home automation, which allows homeowners to control and monitor various devices in their homes using a single platform. The proposed work is an IoT-based Home Automation System using NodeMCU and Blynk IoT App presents a simplified and efficient solution for remote control of home appliances. By leveraging the NodeMCU microcontroller board and the Blynk IoT app, users can conveniently manage their devices from anywhere through their smartphones. The system's architecture involves connecting the NodeMCU board to a relay module, which interfaces with the home appliances. The Blynk IoT app facilitates the creation of switches that correspond to the relay modules, enabling easy on/off control with a simple tap on the smartphone screen. Also, users can control their smart home appliances with voice commands using Google Home. With its minimal component requirements and userfriendly setup, the system offers accessibility to individuals with basic electronics and programming knowledge. Furthermore, the inclusion of a 4 or 6-channel relay module provides flexibility in connecting and controlling multiple devices simultaneously. The proposed system serves as an affordable, accessible, and scalable solution to transform traditional homes into smart and automated environments, enhancing convenience and improving the quality of life for users.

Author Keywords: Internet of Things (IoT, Home Automation System (HAS)

articleTitle: Ensemble Text Classification with TF-IDF Vectorization for Hate Speech Detection in Social Media
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI) has changed how hate speech is detected. In hate speech identification using machine learning, a number of methods are used to automatically find text that uses vocabulary that is considered to be derogatory, discriminatory, or motivated by hatred. Supervised learning techniques like neural networks, decision trees, and SVMs need a labelled dataset comprising samples of hate speech and non-hate speech. This project investigates the use of AI and machine learning techniques to automatically detect material that uses offensive, intolerant, or hostile words. A voting classifier and TF-IDF representations are combined to improve classification accuracy. The ensemble of classifiers, powered by AI approaches, shows impressive accuracy in identifying hate speech by training five different classifiers (Random Forest, Bagging, Support Vector Machine, AdaBoost, and Gradient Boosting) on a labelled dataset of tweets. The TF-IDF representation prioritises textual terms, whereas the ensemble method uses classifier diversity to capture distinctive patterns. Results from experiments show the strategy's effectiveness, with precision 0.95, recall 0.96, f1-score 0.95 and accuracy 0.97 for detecting hate speech. By successfully utilising AI's capacity to fight hate speech, this research helps the development of a diverse and secure online environment. The suggested approach works well for automatically identifying hate speech, making the internet a safer and more welcoming place for all users.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection using CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: The second most common cause of cancer today is a tumour. To detect tumours like brain tumour, the medical field needs a quick, automated, effective, and reliable technique. A crucial part of treatment is detection. Doctors keep a patient out of danger if accurate tumour detection is possible. This application makes use of several image processing methods. Using this application, doctors are able to properly treat a large number of tumour patients and save their lives. Simply put, a tumour is an accumulation of uncontrolledly expanding cells. The development of brain tumour cells causes brain failure because they eventually eat up all the nutrients meant for healthy cells and tissues. To determine the location and size of the patient's brain tumour, doctors manually review the patient's MR images of the brain. This is time-consuming and results in inaccurate tumour detection. A tumour is an uncontrollably expanding mass of tissue. A Deep Learning architecture that combines CNN (Convolution Neural Network), also referred to as NN (Neural Network), and VGG can be used to identify brain tumours. Transfer learning. Its main strength is the model's ability to predict whether a tumor is present in an image. Returning is yes if the cancer is present and no if it is not.

articleTitle: An AI Integrated Emotional Responsive System: Kanmani-The Bot for India
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Virtual assistants have gained a lot of popularity since they simplify many of our jobs, especially during our hectic hours. It is one of the fantastic outcomes of the development of artificial intelligence. It may be improved by including elements for voice emotion recognition to make it more adaptable. As a result, it reduces the amount of time required to type and allows the user to complete the work according to their mood. As a result of our research, in this paper by using Machine Learning, Deep Leaning and artificial intelligence, we developed a model that enables people to interact through video and voice, enhancing the flexibility of a virtual assistant and recognizing emotions and speech, particularly when people want to interact with someone when there is no one around, as well as how valuable it is on a daily basis. The key goal or the main objective is “To empower the minds and ignite the possibilities, by unleashing the future through personalised technology”. I have split KANMANI into three working phrases, the combination of these three phrases will be your virtual companion, which is custom made for your personal world. First is the voice assistant, Artificial intelligence (AI) has made tremendous improvements recently, and its potential grows every day. NLP, often known as natural language processing, is an application field for AI. Voice assistants may converse with people in natural language and include AI, it receives the queries/ commands as speech signals and convert it and give us the output result as speech. Second is the Emotion Identification through speech and facial expression where it identifies the user's emotion and react to it with a quote. Third is the final level the Virtual Assistant, where user can interact through Video with AI that responds to user query with Emotion Detection.

articleTitle: Skin Cancer Detection using Machine Learning and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Skin cancer is a prevalent and potentially lifethreatening disease that requires early detection and timely treatment for improved patient outcomes. In this paper, we address the limitations of traditional approaches to human activity recognition in the context of skin cancer detection. These approaches heavily rely on manual feature extraction, which hinders the generalization model performance and often leads to resource-intensive solutions that are not suitable for smaller datasets or low-specification systems. Furthermore, existing studies primarily focus on classifying skin cancers as benign or malignant, neglecting the differentiation of various types of skin lesions. We propose a sequential model for skin cancer detection, using the VGG16 architecture as the backbone, with additional layers for multi-class classification of skin lesions. Our model aims to deliver an accurate and efficient skin cancer detection system capable of discerning seven distinct types of skin lesions. Implementing this model could lead to early diagnosis and timely treatment of skin cancer, resulting in improved patient outcomes and better public health. By utilizing the VGG16 architecture and emphasizing multiclass classification, our research offers a promising approach to overcome the limitations of manual feature extraction and resource-intensive models.

articleTitle: Ocular Disease Detection Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Prior to the creation of the ophthalmoscope by von Helmholtz roughly 150 years ago, eye doctors had no way of inspecting the area behind the pupil. The recent decade has seen significant development in retinal imaging and image processing, opening up new frontiers in the study of the eye. Prevention of permanent vision loss due to ocular illnesses requires prompt diagnosis. In particular, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown encouraging results in the analysis of medical pictures in recent years. This research provides support for the use of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in the detection of ocular disorders. The proposed method takes retinal fundus images as input and employs a pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) model to extract relevant features. There are a number of benefits to using CNNs to forecast eye diseases instead of more conventional methods. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) can learn complicated characteristics from big datasets, which can boost their accuracy and generalizability. Additionally, they are able to pick up on small changes in medical images that may be ignored by human experts, allowing for earlier diagnosis and treatment of ocular illnesses. Furthermore, CNNs can offer objective and reproducible predictions, which can help to lessen the variability and subjectivity of human evaluations. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are a sort of deep neural network that has shown effective for a number of computer vision tasks. Due to their propensity for learning complicated characteristics from big datasets, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are ideally suited for the analysis of medical pictures like retinal fundus photographs and optical coherence tomography (OCT) images. For the purpose of ocular illness prediction, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are trained using medical image annotation datasets to learn features that can distinguish between healthy and sick eyes. Then, new photos can be analyzed using these traits to determine the existence and severity of ocular disorders. The CNN model was trained and validated using over four thousand fundus images representing various ocular diseases and conditions. Eighty percent of the images were used for training, while the other twenty percent were used for testing. Training using two convolutional layers and two dense layers resulted in an 80% accuracy in predictions.

articleTitle: Design of Energy Efficient BLDC Motor Pump for Agriculture Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: In the realm of residential, commercial, and agricultural applications, conventional pumps have long relied on induction motors. Nevertheless, a notable shift in the sectors like pump systems and electric vehicles where brushless DC (BLDC) motors are increasingly favored over the induction motor. The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) standards primarily revolve around key parameters are discharge (Q), head (H), and power input (Pi), intricately linked to the motor operating speed. In the pursuit of improving overall performance, especially in terms of efficiency, the focus is on enhancing both motor and pump efficiencies. Single-phase induction motors encounter limitations in their efficiency and speed capabilities. In contrast, BLDC motors offer a more versatile and efficient solution, the ability to modulate speed and optimized efficiency make them a superior choice for water pumping in agriculture applications. A BLDC motor with a 1 hp rating, designed to function within a voltage range of 72V and rotate at a speed of 3000 revolutions per minute (rpm), has been proposed as an efficient and effective option for these specific pumping needs. The design and analysis of this BLDC motor are carried out using finite element analysis software MagN et. Through finite element analysis using MagNet software, optimized BLDC motor designs with varying magnet thickness are developed and evaluated, resulting in significant improvements in water discharge capacity, pump head, and overall efficiency when compared to single-phase induction motor-driven pumps. Specifically, there is a 15% increase in both water discharge capacity and pump head. Furthermore, the overall conversion efficiency experiences a significant enhancement, ranging from 7% within the nominal operating head range.

articleTitle: Identification of Brain Tumor Stages and Brain Tumor Diagnosis Using Deep Learning Model Based on Inception V4 and DENSENET 201
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: One of the most fatal illnesses is a brain tumor, and identifying it is a difficult task for medical professionals due to the heterogeneous structure of its cells. Usually, MRI images are used to detect the brain tumor. The current approach has some issues classifying brain tumors in the existing system, and its prediction accuracy is also quite poor. To address these issues, Hybridization of Inception v4 and Densenet201 helps to identify the brain tumor. We classify the brain tumor and assess its classification using these two models. For the classification of brain tumors, Inception modules from pre-trained Inception v4 were extracted, then Densenet201 concatenated these characteristics. Following feature extraction and concatenation, these features were forwarded to the classifier. The results show that the feature concatenation method, which uses a deep learning model that has already been trained, performs better.

articleTitle: Malware Detection Using 1d Convolution with Batch Normalization and L2 Regularization for Android
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Mobile applications on Android have become the most frequently targeted platform. This puts the users at a significant security risk against malware. Incorporation of machine learning techniques for detecting malware has been widely studied in the past decade. Most of the Android malware detectors with deep learning approach are defined using two dimensional convolutions networks that are specifically designed for image data. The nature of malware data is different from image in terms of input data shape. The dependency on two dimensional convolutions enhances the computational requirement of android malware classifiers. To reduce computational demand and complexity of a deep learning binary classification model, a light weight and efficient approach is proposed. This approach involves one-dimensional convolution, batch normalization layers, and L2 kernel regularization. It operates directly on the entire APK file and requires less computation with less number of hidden layers and enables the detection of malicious applications even before their execution.

articleTitle: A LSTM Deep Learning method with Attention Dense Mechanism for AQI prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Accurate prediction of PM2.5 concentrations is crucial in addressing the severe air pollution issues faced by countries like India. In this study, we propose a comprehensive algorithm that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), attention mechanisms, and dense layers for PM2.5 prediction while incorporating meteorological features specific to the Indian context. To evaluate the algorithm's performance on Indian data, we collected a large dataset consisting of historical PM2.5 concentrations and associated meteorological features from monitoring stations across India. The dataset underwent preprocessing, including normalization and scaling, to ensure consistent input ranges for the models. Through experimental comparisons among the CNN, LSTM, CNN-LSTM, and CNN-LSTM-Attention-Dense algorithms using the Indian dataset, our findings demonstrated that the CNN-LSTM-AttentionDense algorithm outperformed the other algorithms, exhibiting the highest prediction accuracy for PM2.5 concentrations in the Indian context. By harnessing the spatial and temporal capabilities of CNNs and LSTMs, coupled with attention mechanisms and dense layers, our proposed algorithm effectively captured the intricate patterns and relationships between Indian meteorological conditions and PM2.5 concentrations. The integration of attention mechanisms enabled the model to focus on the meteorological features with significant impacts on air quality in the Indian context. This research contributes to the development of accurate PM2.5 prediction models tailored specifically to the unique meteorological characteristics of India. The outcomes of this work have practical implications for policymakers, environmental agencies, and individuals in India, enabling proactive decision-making and mitigation strategies to combat the adverse effects of air pollution and safeguard public health.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Ethanol Detection System: A Transformative Stride in Ensuring Food Authenticity
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: In the present era, the rapid rise of IoT technology has brought forth innovative solutions, particularly in ensuring food safety. This study introduces an IoT-based ethanol detection system tailored to preserve the quality and security of food products. Ethanol, a key indicator of food spoilage, can endanger consumer well-being in excessive amounts. Food adulteration with hazardous substances like ethanol poses a serious public health challenge; the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) reported that 30% of tested food samples (2017-2019) exceeded safe ethanol levels. Addressing this, we present an IoTbased Ethanol Detection System (IoTEDS), merging sensitive ethanol sensors and IoT tech. IoTEDS monitors ethanol levels in real-time across the food supply chain, enabling remote data analysis and swift risk detection. Through advanced algorithms, the system processes sensor data, generating precise alerts to prevent compromised product distribution. This tech enhances food safety, cuts losses, and safeguards public health. By incorporating touch-sensitive ethanol sensors with IoT capabilities, this research pioneers modern quality assurance, fostering transparent supply chains and industry accountability. IoTEDS’ real-time monitoring, data analysis, and risk mitigation position it as a transformative stride in ensuring food authenticity.

articleTitle: The Synergy of Advanced Language Models, Sequential Skeleton Features, and GAN-Enhanced Data Augmentation for Unprecedented Precision
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: The precision comparison between the proposed method and traditional methods is a crucial evaluation of their performance in machine learning and information retrieval tasks. Precision, a fundamental metric, measures the accuracy of positive predictions. This study presents the “Proposed Method,” an innovative approach, alongside “Traditional Methods,” representing conventional approaches. The comparison, visualized in a precision-focused diagram, demonstrates how effectively each method identifies relevant instances. A higher precision value in the Proposed Method implies its proficiency in minimizing false positives, particularly vital in precision-critical applications like medical diagnosis and spam email classification. This analysis aids stakeholders and researchers in assessing the precision-related trade-offs between innovation and convention, guiding informed decisions for specific contexts.

articleTitle: Fish Farm Monitoring System Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Fish aquaculture is an essential sector of the economy; it has seen rapid expansion in recent years. It can be challenging to manage a fish farm, though, as it demands continual attention to environmental parameters like water quality and temperature. In this study, we offer a monitoring system for fish farms that leverages IoT technology to gather and process data from sensors placed inside a fish farm. When any parameters are outside the specified range, the system notifies the farmer and provides real-time monitoring of water quality, temperature, and other environmental conditions. The method comprises a network of wireless sensors connected to a central computer and installed across the fish farm. The server gathers and analyses the sensor data before giving the farmer real-time access via a web-based interface. The fish farmer can utilize this interface to keep an eye on the fish farm's water quality and temperature as well as to change the feeding schedule and other environmental factors as needed. The system has undergone testing in a commercial fish farm, and the outcomes indicate that it successfully keeps track of the environmental conditions there. The technology can increase fish farming's productivity and profitability while minimizing its adverse environmental effects.

articleTitle: An Efficient Method for Leaf Diseases Detection Using Deep Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Leaf diseases identification and sorting are essential responsibilities in crops, and they pose a significant challenge in today's agriculture and food processing environments since they affect crop inputs and yields. A more accurate and timelier prognosis of agricultural leaf diseases could aid in the creation of an immediate corrective method, greatly reducing economic and production losses. Deep learning technical developments have enabled investigators to significantly improve the performance and accuracy of object identification and recognition systems. The primary objective is to establish how to come up with a more applicable neural network framework for the stated duties. In the present article, we put forward the use of a convolutional neural network (CNN) approach for detecting crop leaf diseases in an assortment of plants employing images taken from plant leaves. As a result, it is able to appropriately assess the detection and classification processes. The proposed crop leaf disease forecasts include four stages: preprocessing to enhance and shrink images using the contrast stretching approach; segmentation using k-means clustering technique; feature extraction and classification using convolutional neural networks. Following that, we detected and displayed in the conversation box several segmentation features, classifier performance metrics, and statistical and structural features of the anticipated disease type. Finally, the acquired findings were compared to existing methodologies, and it was determined that the proposed plant disease prediction method is both accurate and efficient.

articleTitle: Cofee Quality Prediction Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: The analysis and modeling of a dataset related to sensory evaluations of coffee quality scores is presented in this report. The report explores various features related to aroma, flavor, aftertaste, acidity, body, balance, uniformity, cleanliness, sweetness, and overall quality of coffee. The report starts with data preprocessing, including handling missing values and encoding categorical variables. The report then drops irrelevant columns and extracts useful information from date columns. For the modeling phase, the report splits the data into training and testing sets and applies feature scaling using the MinMaxScaler to normalize the numeric features. The report then trains a Linear Regression model and evaluates its performance using mean squared error (MAE) and R- squared score. The model achieved a low MAE of 0.2567 and a high R-squared score of 0. 9476, indicating a good fit to the data. Furthermore, the report compares the performance of various regression models using cross-validation. The models included Linear Regression, Ridge, Lasso, ElasticNet, Decision Tree Regressor, Random Forest Regressor, Gradient Boosting Regressor, Support Vector Regressor (SVR), and MLP Regressor. Finally, the report recommends the best coffee combination based on the analysis. The recommended coffee combination is from Coffee Quality Union, with the variety of Castillo, the country of origin of Colombia, the farm name of Finca El Paraiso, and the processing method of Double Anaerobic Washed.

articleTitle: Predicting Average Tomato Prices Using Support Vector Machine with Polynomial Features
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Every economy depends on agriculture, and research in this area is primarily focused on boosting food supply and quality while minimizing costs and maximizing profit. Numerous factors can have an impact on tomato pricing, which serve as a crucial indicator of market trends for vegetables. Making educated decisions could be facilitated by predicting tomato average prices. To forecast the typical prices of tomatoes, we used the Support Vector Machine (SVM) model together with polynomial feature modification in this study. For our projections, we used the ‘Minimum’ and ‘Maximum’ pricing attributes. To guarantee consistency and improved performance, the dataset was standardized. With crossvalidation, we used a Grid Search technique to refine the parameters of our SVM model. The Mean Squared Error (MSE) and R2 score metrics were used to assess the model's performance. Our findings were shown graphically by scatter plots that contrasted real and forecasted prices and a histogram that showed the prediction errors. The SVM model has the potential to forecast average tomato prices when used in conjunction with polynomial feature transformation and parameter optimization. The agricultural industry's stakeholders may use this technique to gather knowledge of price trends and guide their decisions. More research may be done to increase prediction accuracy by incorporating more features and using other algorithm.

articleTitle: Quick Response Codes for Bone Fracture Diagnosis Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Orthopaedic treatment and a precise diagnosis of bone fractures are essential components of contemporary healthcare. This study introduces a novel method for streamlining and improving the analyses of bone fractures through the use of QR codes and object detection methods. In this study, we present a novel technique to increase the speed and precision of bone fracture diagnosis by integrating computer vision skills with QR code technology. The workflow of the system starts with the gathering of digital medical pictures, such as X-rays or CT scans, which are afterwards tagged with QR codes that are patient specific. To locate fractures in these photos and to identify them, a deep learning-based on fracture detection model is used. The method is also well suited for telemedicine applications, enabling distant specialists to offer quick assessments. Additionally, the gathered information can be used for orthopaedic care research and initiatives to enhance quality of care. We demonstrate the system's efficacy and emphasize its potential to revolutionize orthopaedics through thorough examination and case studies. We think that the combination of object detection with QR codes can greatly improve the speed and precision of bone fracture diagnosis, leading to better patient outcomes overall. With a direct bearing on patient care and the medical community's capacity to offer prompt and accurate diagnoses in orthopaedic patients, this research represents a significant advancement in the merging of medical imaging technology with artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Convolution Neural Network for Gastrointestinal Cancer Detection and Classification using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Ailments of the gastrointestinal tract (GIT), including bleeding, ulcers, polyps, Crohn's disease, and cancer, are becoming more prevalent. Ulcers and bleeding in the small and large bowels are two of them that are particularly common. Medical experts find the manual diagnostic process to be both time-consuming and difficult. As a result, experts have suggested computerised techniques for the identification and classification of certain disorders. Medical video endoscopy produces a huge volume of images, thus it takes a long time for specialists to look over them all. Early detection and diagnosis of certain illnesses can result in successful therapy. SqueezeNet, ResNet-101, and DenseNet-169 are three deep learning-based models that we introduce in this paper and assess for their capacity to diagnose a dataset of lower gastrointestinal disorders. There are 5,000 images in the Kvasir dataset, similarly distributed among five different lower gastrointestinal conditions, including ulcerative colitis, polyps, normal cecum, and normal pylorus. The deep feature vector is processed using the softmax activation function, which divides the input images into five groups. Surprisingly, all of the convolutional neural network (CNN) models had exceptional performance, with DenseNet-169 reaching accuracy, specificity, precision, recall, and F1 Score values of 97.8%, 98.07%, 97.5%, 96.02% and 97.6%.

articleTitle: Design of a Smart Energy Meter and Monitoring System for Industrial and Residential Use Based on the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Electronic meters have become increasingly important for efficient energy use, and the proposed research aims to develop an IoT-based architecture for metering and monitoring. This smart monitoring and control system (SMACS) for home appliances is suggested to enhance household electricity control. The technology uses a wireless control module with an ESP8266 microcontroller and Wi-Fi channel to monitor current consumption and send measured amounts over Wi-Fi. The system calculates current consumption, counts units, and displays results on the user's website and smartphone. It avoids using traditional analog and digital meter reading techniques and allows remote access to electronic meters. The proposed work offers lower total costs, greater energy savings, and reduced time and labour requirements.

articleTitle: Detection of DDOS Attacks in Cloud Environment Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: The rapid evolution of cloud computing and the increasing reliance on Software -Defined Networking (SDN) have introduced new challenges in ensuring the security and availability of cloud based services. Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, in particular, pose a significant threat to the stability and performance of cloud infrastructures. As network traffic patterns continue to increase and evolve, it is crucial to extract pertinent features that aid in identifying attacks and improving the accuracy of detection. Therefore, effective detection mechanisms are crucial to identify and mitigate DDoS attacks in SDN-based cloud environments. This study presents a novel approach that combines Decision Tree with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) for effective DDoS detection in cloud infrastructures. The model is evaluated using the 2019 dataset. The simulation findings validateits efficacy and show that it improves upon existing works in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: Novel Implementation of Heart Disease Classification Model using RNN Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Heart disease is the major health issue or challenge faced by the entire world in modern medicine. It has become a crucial factor for increasing the mortality rate. The desperation of heart disease is more vital and can even result in vulnerable consequences if it is not predicted at the initial stage. The methods such as electronic health records, monitoring body are network continuously and diagnosing the patient health condition via the medical sensors projection and wearable device across human bodies. Since the generated data from the human body are continuous and huge in amount, the data mining techniques are utilised for efficient classification of obtained health data. Moreover, the classification of health data is the most critical process as it needs an accurate execution with the early detection of heart disease. As most medical enthusiasts and practicing physicians finding reveals that difficult to diagnose the disease at an early stage is the key for the failures of incurable disease. Hence it is important to diagnose patients early to save life is the most challenging task for the medical fraternity. This research proposes to reduce the risk of heart diseases by effective feature selection and classification based prediction system to predict heart diseases. Therefore, the earlier prediction of heart disease with higher accuracy is an important limitation behind every existing process. So, this research attempts to develop an efficient classifier and predicts heart disease at the initial stage with highperformance measures and accuracy. The significant contribution of this research is divided into three parts. First, an effective method is implemented to predict heart disease by feature selection and classification. The proposed research comprises of optimised unsupervised technique for feature selection and novel MLP-EBMDA (Multi-Layer Perceptron for Enhanced Brownian Motion-based Dragonfly Algorithm) for classification for heart disease prediction. In this implementation, the input will be obtained from the dataset and performed pre-processing followed by the proposed feature selection technique that efficiently performs the selection of features. Based on selected features, heart disease classification vi is performed using novel MLP-EBMDA that helps to predict heart disease at the initial stage. This suggested system possesses an accuracy rate of 94.28 percentage in predicting heart disease as normal or abnormal in an effective way.

articleTitle: MXDD Scheduling Algorithm for MIBC Switches
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Scheduling multicast traffic is the emerging research area due to increased growth and use of the multicast applications on the Internet. This work focuses on the multicast scheduling for M×N Internally Buffered Crossbar Switches. Internally Buffered Crossbar (IBC) switches, then again, have been considered a powerful option in contrast to buffer less crossbar switches to improve the scheduling execution. The Multicast Cross-point Due Date multicast scheduling algorithm (MXDD) is proposed with an input and output scheduling. In input scheduling the HOL of the all the input ports is transferred to the corresponding buffer at each cross point. The output scheduling has two phases for getting the fairness and alleviate the HOL blocking and Starvation problem. In phase I, The Due Date is assigned to the cells in the buffer at each cross-point. In Phase II, the cells which are assigned Due Date 1 are allowed to be scheduled in the N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> time Slot. This scheme appears to deal with multicast traffic more proficiently and far superior to conventional schemes. However, MXDD is both down to earth and accomplishes superior.

articleTitle: Regression Method-Based Prediction of Wind Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Wind power prediction is essential in tackling the challenges of balancing supply and demand in any electrical system, given the uncertainty surrounding the output of wind farms. To cut emissions and encourage sustainable growth, certain countries have recently shifted to renewable energy sources, particularly wind and solar energy. Given that renewable energy sources are incorporated into already-existing grids and blended with conventional sources, determining the amount of electricity that will be produced is crucial to minimising the wind farm's operational costs and guaranteeing the power grid's safety. Accurate wind power projections help to reduce the need for extra reserve and balancing power to incorporate wind power. With the help of machine learning (ML) techniques and historical wind power generation data, this system provides a prediction model to address a real-world problem in the field of renewable energy. It accurately predicts the quantity of wind energy production each hour during the following 24 hours. Since meteorological conditions are unpredictable, wind power generated by wind turbines cannot be planned. So, in order to conduct activities such as energy trading, load tracking, pre-load sharing, turbine control, and others, wind power forecasts are required. Data mining is a commonly used approach for analysing enormous amounts of data in all fields. Researchers employ a variety of data mining and machine learning techniques to analyse massive, complex environmental data and help experts forecast the generation of wind power. The proposed method entails developing a machine learning model that can forecast power generation. When evaluating alternative regression algorithms, the decision tree is the most effective model for outcome prediction.

articleTitle: Enabling Energy Efficient Communication between Entities Using 5G Assisted Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Most of the sensor nodes in WSNs rely on power sources, which have a finite lifespan and can adversely influence the network's functionality, excellence and longevity because of the amount of energy they place on each node. Thus, several clustering approaches are proposed to enhance WSNs' energy efficiency. Mobile communication technology has completely altered the way individuals interact with one another. Providers of internet services now face difficulties due to the exponential growth in the amount of users, the speed of data transfer, the need for more bandwidth, and the volume of data being sent. The expectation is that the contemporary communication system will fulfill all these needs. Next-generation communication technologies will prioritize the creation of user terminals that mix several flows from different technologies and enable access to those technologies. The researchers of this work have offered a comprehensive summary of the current state of wireless communication technologies and their potential for future improvement. This transmission is energy intensive. There has been a rise in the number of users necessitating constant connection due to the transition from 4G, which is transformed to 4G with LTE in wireless communication. Because of this, battery life on mobile devices is shortened. Therefore, a strategy should be created to reduce consumption of energy, which will lengthen the life of portable packs of batteries. A fifth-Generation (5G) technological advance, which is discussed in this article, is discussed, and it is both intelligent and interconnected with the rest of the world. In addition, this paper addresses the limitations of current wireless technology, the problems with current cellular networks, and the necessity for the next-generation communication technologies. In addition, 5G wireless communication has been the subject of extensive research and discussion. The major concern of this paper is to prove the efficiency of the proposed work by means of the improvements in the following metrics such as: throughput, energy efficiency, reduced delay and improved Frame Success Ratio (FSR).

articleTitle: The Confluence of Edge Computing and Artificial Neural Networks for Real-time Data Processing in IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: In this study, we present a novel approach for efficient real-time data processing in IoT devices at the edge by dynamically adapting artificial neural networks (ANNs) based on available computational resources and input data complexity. We address the challenges of resource constraints and latency reduction, crucial for enabling seamless and responsive IoT applications. Our proposed method comprises three main algorithms: Dynamic Neural Network Adaptation (DNNA), Edge Inference Scheduler (EIS), and Latency-aware Activation Thresholding (LAT). Algorithm 1, DNNA, is responsible for dynamically adjusting the complexity of the deployed ANN to match the available resources and data complexity. It optimizes the trade-off between computational efficiency and model accuracy, making the best use of limited edge resources. Algorithm 2, EIS, optimizes the allocation of computational resources while minimizing latency during task scheduling on edge devices. It ensures that tasks are assigned to devices that can meet latency requirements, improving overall system responsiveness. Algorithm 3, LAT, dynamically adjusts activation thresholds within ANNs based on predicted latency, allowing for a fine balance between accuracy and processing speed. This adaptation ensures that the ANN performs optimally under varying conditions. Our experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over traditional approaches in terms of latency, inference accuracy, energy efficiency, scalability, privacy, security, resource utilization, and overall efficiency. The proposed method not only reduces latency but also maintains high accuracy levels, making it a valuable solution for real-time data processing in IoT devices at the edge.

articleTitle: Exploration of Smart Medical Systems for Efficient Recognition of Potential Sleep Disruption Cases Relying on Health Metrics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: This study explores a state-of-the-art methodology for the efficient recognition of potential sleep disruption cases relying on health metrics, comparing it with six traditional methods. The proposed method combines wearable technology, advanced data analysis, and machine learning to continuously monitor and analyze a wide range of health metrics during sleep. The traditional methods include Polysomnography (PSG), Actigraphy, Electroencephalography (EEG) analysis, Sleep Questionnaires, Sleep Diary, and Actigraph Monitoring. The comparison is made based on performance parameters, accessibility, and cost efficiency. Results indicate that the Proposed Method outperforms the traditional methods in all key performance parameters - sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. The Proposed Method achieves a high sensitivity of 0.96, ensuring it correctly identifies a vast majority of sleep disruption cases, while maintaining a specificity of 0.93 to minimize false alarms. The accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score are consistently higher for the Proposed Method, affirming its superior accuracy and reliability. Furthermore, the Proposed Method exhibits notable advantages in terms of accessibility and cost efficiency. It is highly accessible, leveraging widely available wearable devices and mobile applications, enabling real-time monitoring and continuous tracking of health metrics. This accessibility, coupled with its cost-effectiveness, offers a user-friendly and economical solution for individuals and healthcare providers. In conclusion, the proposed methodology, with its emphasis on smart medical systems and advanced data analytics, presents a significant leap forward in the field of sleep disruption recognition. Its performance and accessibility surpass traditional methods, making it a valuable tool for early detection and personalized intervention in sleep-related disorders. The methodology is poised to enhance the overall management of sleep disruption cases, ultimately contributing to improved well-being.

articleTitle: Boosting Accuracy in Rice Leaf Disease Classification with a CNN-RF Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: The research paper's results for classifying rice leaf diseases employing precision, recall, and The F1-S metrics have been briefly summarised in the abstract. To correctly identify different rice leaf diseases, such as bacterial blight, bacterial leaf streak, blasting (leaf and collar), brown location, false smut, rice grassy stunt, paddy tattered stunt, and sheath blight, they used a classification model in this study. The performance metrics for the model for each illness class can be seen in the table. For each disease category, precision-recall and F1-Score serve as key metrics to evaluate the model's classification accuracy. The precision of a model's ability to properly identify cases of a certain disease is measured by the proportion of genuine positive predictions among all positive predictions. Recall measures the proportion of accurate positive predictions among all real positive instances and illustrates how well the model detects diseases. The F1-Score provides a fair assessment of the model's overall performance in classification by balancing precision and recall. The results highlight the model's ability to correctly classify rice leaf illnesses and show consistently good precision, recall, and overall F1-Score scores throughout all disease classes, which range from roughly 90.23% to 94.59%. The sizable-support values, which represent the number of occurrences for each illness class and the overall distribution in the data set among different categories, provide substantial support for these measures. The model's general success is further summarised by the macro alongside weighted average statistics, which show an impressive average reliability, recollection, and F1-Score of about 93.51% on average, demonstrating the model's consistency and high accuracy in analyzing rice leaf diseases through the entire dataset.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Examination of Cloud-Enabled Frameworks for Power Management Systems: Current State, Challenges, and Forward-Looking Guidance in Big Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: A Comprehensive Examination of Cloud-Enabled Frameworks for Power Management Systems: Current State, Challenges, and Forward-Looking Guidance in Big Data Analytics” examines cloud-enabled power management system frameworks in depth. This article provides a thorough evaluation of cloud-enabled power management system frameworks. This article examines the present state of power management systems from a range of perspectives. It emphasizes the importance of shifting away from traditional, locally focused methodologies and toward big data analytics-driven, cloud-based solutions. In this study, we look at the wide-ranging implications that cloud-enabled frameworks have had on a variety of sectors, including smart grids and data centers. It is hard to exaggerate the significance of these frameworks in handling the exponential expansion of data while also improving efficiency, scalability, and adaptability. This research acknowledges the relevance of data security and privacy, the necessity for interoperability and standardization in this rapidly expanding environment, and the difficulty in managing the huge volumes of data created by contemporary energy systems. This is achieved while stressing the numerous benefits of cloud-hosted data centers and intelligent grids. The paper also underlines how advantageous cloud-based data centers and smart grids are to their respective users. The essay proposes potential solutions to these difficulties in the form of future recommendations.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning for Real-time ICU Patient Management in Critical Care
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Managing patients, especially in high-stakes environments like intensive care units (ICUs), is a difficult and time-sensitive task. Reinforcement learning, or RL, has the potential to greatly enhance the health of patients and the efficiency with which existing resources are used in the administration of real-time intensive care unit patients. To prove the superiority of the RL-based methodology, we compare the results of our RL-based method to those of more conventional methodologies. The proposed method combines the Actor-Critical architecture for continuous actions with a baseline value estimate and Q-Learning for selecting discrete actions. Policy Gradient is proposed for controlling continuous activities. Treatment choices for ICU patients can be optimized using this mix of algorithms because of their robustness and flexibility. Results from simulations reveal that the RL-based strategy consistently outperforms the traditional techniques in terms of key performance criteria such patient outcome improvement, resource efficiency, treatment response time, adverse event avoidance, patient satisfaction, and cost savings. In addition to improving patient care and healthcare resource allocation, this study demonstrates that RL has the potential to transform real-time patient management in intensive care units. Maximizing the effectiveness with which patients are cared for in the ICU is of paramount importance in the dynamic field of critical care. Using reinforcement learning (RL), this study introduces a novel approach to the treatment of ICU patients in real time. To enhance patient outcomes, resource utilization efficiency, and overall cost savings, the proposed method employs RL algorithms to encourage data-driven decision-making. We test our RL-based technique against six traditional methods and show that it outperforms them all.

Author Keywords: improved patient outcomes. The Keywords Are Resource Efficiency

articleTitle: Estimation of Bus Arrival by Tracking and Analyzing the Users Real Time Location
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: High level business strategies are continuously being improved by changes in innovation. In the system, a number of methods have been shown to enhance the comfort and health of people's daily lives. The paper's major goal is to use cutting-edge GPS and IoT in Intelligent Transportation Systems. The bus could have been delayed for several reasons. Clogged roads, malfunctions, and bad weather are examples of these. People waiting at bus stops have no idea of the bus's delay or arrival time. These issues can be addressed by using Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) that use GPS and IoT in mobile applications to allow passengers to track the locations of their bus in real time They may also check the Estimated Time of Arrival of a certain bus, which is derived using machine learning techniques and takes into account environmental changes as well as other aspects such as traffic density and weather conditions, and follow their bus positions in real time. The main scope of this intelligent mobile app is to display the current area of a client's separate transportation in Google Maps along with the It is a Real-time tracking as if the source address of the transport is restored every second as scope of latitudes and longitudes, which are gained by customers by their app with the assistance of the Google Map API. This system can effectively address the problems related to bus timing transparency and arrival time forecasting. The buses are equipped with a real-time vehicle tracking module containing Real-time tracking with Transport global positioning (TPS). The traffic congestion in the current location of the bus and weather data are some of the factors used for the ETA prediction using the Distance Matrix API.

articleTitle: A Study Of Cyclone Tracking Mechanism Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: With over 90 storms emerging worldwide each year, tropical cyclones (TCs) are the most damaging weather systems to emerge over the tropical oceans. For the purpose of providing advanced warning to the impacted areas, fast TC detection and tracking is essential. Remote sensing is essential for the detection of these storms since they originate over open oceans that are far from the continents. Here, we describe an innovative deep learning approach-based automated technique for TC detection from satellite photos. Our research presents a three-phase deep learning architecture for TC detection that consists of three components: 1) a classifier—convolutional neural network (CNN); 2) a wind speed filter; and 3) a detector—Mask convolutional neural network (CNN). Using Bayesian optimization, the hyperparameters of the pipeline as a whole are tuned to display optimal performance. Results show that the suggested method produces test images with specificity (97.59%), high precision (97.10%) and accuracy (86.55%).

articleTitle: Improving Onion Leaf Disease Diagnosis With a CNN-Random Forest Classification Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: This study proposes a disease diagnosis system for onion leaves that uses an amalgamation of Convolutional Neural Networks, and Random Forest. Damping off, Violet blotch, Stemphylium plant blight, Fusarium bottom rot, Pink rot of the roots, and Black mold constitute the main onion leaf diseases targeted by the model. The model's performance is assessed using major machine learning measures such as Precision, and recall. and F1-Score, as well as assistance and assistance proportion for each illness class. The results show that the suggested model is effective, with good accuracy rates for symptom classification. The Damping off class, for example, achieved an accuracy of 91.50%, a remember of 82.35%, having an F1 score of 86.69% with 850 instances and an encouragement proportion of 0.15. Similarly, with 926 occurrences and a support percentage of 0.17, the Purple Blotches class earned a level of accuracy of 87.22%, remember of 76.67%, with an F1-Score of 81.61%. The total performance is represented by the Macro Average, which has an average accuracy of 71.34%, remember of 78.07%, with F1-Score of 80.48%. The model's robustness is further validated by the Weighted Average, which has average accuracy, recollections, and F1-Score of 85.40%, 86.00%, and 84.90%, respectively. Furthermore, the Small Sample Average has a continuous recall, precision, and F1 score of 78.00%, confirming the model's capacity to diagnose onion leaf illnesses. The suggested CNN-Random Forest model has excellent application potential in onion crop management. The model's precise disease categorization capabilities can considerably improve disease detection and preventative tactics, ultimately leading to increased agricultural yield and quality. These findings have important ramifications for agriculture, providing vital insights for efficient control of disease practices in onion cultivation.

articleTitle: Automated Pest Classification and Infestation Detection using CNN and Transfer Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Traditional agricultural practices have historically been the bedrock for maximizing crop production in the agricultural sector, which now plays a crucial role in maintaining food supply. Deep le arning approaches, however, have become more well-known in the context of modern research due to their success in classifying a variety of image data. In this study, we use Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to identify and categories nine different pest groups that are frequent in common crops. We carefully use image augmentation techniques to solve the difficulties of handling large datasets. We rigorously assess the accuracy and performance of the many convolutional neural network designs that are incorporated into the architectural configurations of our CNN models. Additionally, we use transfer learning strategies into the framework for the study of the pest dataset in order to improve our strategy. A comparison of the CNN-based approach and transfer learning, specifically using pre-existing architectural models, highlights an important conclusion, which is that the combination of CNN and transfer learning results in a remarkable testing accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$98{{\% }}$</tex>. This outcome, which was attained by training on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$80{{\% }}$</tex> of the data and testing on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20{{\% }}$</tex> of the data, highlights the method's strong potential.

articleTitle: Generating and Defending Against Adversarial Examples for Loan Eligibility Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the critical problem of generating and defending against adversarial examples in the context of loan eligibility prediction. Adversarial examples are deliberately crafted inputs that are designed to deceive machine learning models, and they pose a significant risk to the accuracy of loan approval decisions. We explore a variety of adversarial attacks, such as poison and evasion attacks, and their potential implications for loan eligibility prediction models. The Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) is proposed as a technique to generate adversarial examples, and its effectiveness is evaluated on a variety of loan eligibility prediction models. Additionally, we assess the efficacy of different defense strategies to counter adversarial attacks. Our findings highlight the alarming effectiveness of adversarial attacks in causing model misclassifications, and they establish FGSM as a powerful tool for generating adversarial examples. Furthermore, our research underscores the importance of implementing robust defenses to mitigate the impact of adversarial examples in loan eligibility prediction. It is our hope that our work will stimulate further research into this important area of machine learning security as a valuable contribution to this field.

articleTitle: Investigations on Wind Driven PMSG Based Power Generation Scheme for Telecom Tower
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: This paper presents a novel integrated hybrid power supply solution designed to address the concerns of the telecom industry, including rising Operational Expenditure (OPEX) and carbon emissions due to grid electricity and Diesel Generators (DG) dependency. The solution impacts renewable Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS) as the primary power source, supported by a secondary battery backup, to power Base Transceiver Stations (BTS). The chosen configuration employs a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG) with a diode bridge rectifier, known for its reliability and cost-effectiveness. To optimize wind energy capture from varying wind speeds cost-effectively and ensure practical implementation, a hysteresis voltage controller-based buck converter was developed. This controller is notable for its simplicity, affordability in design and implementation, and robust performance against disturbances from both the wind source and load variations. Comprehensive simulations are conducted using the MATLAB Simulink environment to validate the hysteresis voltage controller's performance in providing power to telecom towers via a PMSG-based system. Additionally, a laboratory prototype capable of delivering <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.2{{\ kW}}$</tex> of power is developed and rigorously tested.

articleTitle: Hand Detection and Morse Code Translation for Alternative Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: This paper focuses on developing a real-time Morse code translation system using finger movements captured by a camera and processed with the MediaPipe framework. To enable this, the paper compares the performance of three hand detection algorithms: Yolov5, RetinaNet, and Detectron 2, and identifies MediaPipe as the most effective method for hand tracking. The proposed approach provides a practical and accessible communication method for individuals with speech disorders and opens up new opportunities for improved communication in various settings. The novelty of this work lies in the combination of hand detection algorithms and Morse code translation to develop a robust and efficient communication system for those with speech disorders. Overall, this study highlights the potential of Assistive Speech Technologies in improving communication and promoting inclusion for individuals with speech disorders.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Survey of Machine Learning Strategies for Tumor Classification using Gene Expression Profiling
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Significant progress has been made in the field of tumor classification utilizing gene expression profiling in recent years. This research paper explores the potential of machine learning methods for tumor classification and suggests this approach as an alternative to current methods of diagnosis. The key performance measures used to evaluate these methods are the F1 score, accuracy, precision, recall, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC), and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-PR). The proposed approach was put to the test alongside many others utilizing a dataset of gene expression profiles, including DecisionTree, K-Nearest Neighbors, Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, and Principal Component Analysis. It was established that the proposed technique outperformed the alternatives. The study shows that the newly suggested method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in every respect, demonstrating its superior accuracy and precision in tumor classification. Furthermore, the current method is notably more computationally efficient, requiring only two hours of computing time as opposed to the significantly longer amounts of time spent calculating by earlier approaches. In conclusion, our results emphasize the relevance of the proposed technique for future tumor classification studies. Its excellent processing efficiency and outstanding accuracy make it a viable tool for precise categorization of tumor subtypes based on gene expression data. This study also emphasizes the significance of deliberative decision-making when selecting and evaluating machine learning algorithms for use in biomedical applications. New methods for enhancing tumor classification are made possible by our research, and this in turn aids in the development of more accurate diagnoses, prognoses, and tailored treatment programs for patients.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Technique for Prognosticating Crop Yield Variability with Air Quality Index
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Rice production in India holds significant importance in terms of its contribution to the economy and food security. However, the expansion of this sector is currently facing challenges due to the increasing levels of air pollution, including ground-level ozone and particle matter. The objective of this study is to examine the influence of air quality index (AQI) factors on rice productivity, namely during the winter season, with a particular emphasis on the exceptional year of 2020-2021. By utilizing Internet of Things (IoT) technology, the collection of real-time air quality data is combined with rice yield analysis through the implementation of decision tree regression, k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and support vector regression (SVR) methods. The research findings emphasis the effectiveness of the decision tree model in accurately representing the complex relationship between AQI and rice yield. This model demonstrates higher predictive accuracy when compared to SVR and KNN. This study highlights the importance of managing air quality in order to achieve sustainable rice production. Additionally, it emphasizes the potential of monitoring systems based on the Internet of Things (IoT) to significantly transform agricultural practices. By doing so, these systems may effectively connect environmental stewardship, technological innovation, and food security.

articleTitle: Enhancing Irrigation Efficiency with AI-Based Instinctive Irrigation System (IIS) in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: An AI-assisted intuitive irrigation system built on Arduino and Zigbee that operates within a wireless sensor network is an example of an innovative application of technology in the field of agriculture. This technology enhances the process of watering in real time by utilizing sensors, microcontrollers, a wireless connection, and algorithmic programs that are powered by artificial intelligence. An open-source microcontroller platform serves as the “brains” of the system, receiving data from a wide variety of sensors and using that information to direct the operation of the irrigation system. The Arduino and the nodes that contain the sensors are connected by means of a bridge that is formed by the wireless connection module. In the field, numerous kinds of sensors are used to measure a wide variety of properties, including soil moisture, air temperature, relative humidity, and light intensity, to name just a few of these factors. The artificial intelligence program receives data from the sensors, and it uses that data to make judicious judgments regarding the amount of water to apply to the plants. A solenoid valve and a pump are only two examples of the types of gear that are utilized in irrigation systems to regulate the flow of water. They can be powered on using the Arduino if desired. When constructing wireless sensor networks, it is crucial to keep energy saving in mind as one of the important issues to consider about. ZigBee is a significant advancement in technology that contributes to the resolution of this complex problem. Through the utilization of wireless sensor networks and monitoring systems, the primary objective of this research is to advance our comprehension of data transmission via wireless media. The development of a fully automated irrigation system suitable for usage in Pennsylvania is the primary objective of this research. The regulation of temperature, the amount of moisture in the soil, and the level of humidity in the air are the three key parameters that will be of assistance in the achievement of this objective.

articleTitle: Fuzz_OSR: Fuzzy based Optimal Secured Route selection model in Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks for efficient data transmission
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks (UWSNs) investigate the aquatic environment to provide different underwater surveillance applications. The distinctive characteristics of UWSN, however, also provide additional difficulties, including as constrained bandwidth, significant propagation delays, mobile node behavior, and high error rates. The vulnerability of UWSNs to assaults is further exacerbated by their deployment in unsupervised environments. Due to these difficulties, security solutions for Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) are not practicable for use with UWSN. Through hacked sensor nodes, adversaries conduct fake report injection attacks and false vote injection assaults. False reports may be found and filtered out throughout the multi-hop forwarding process using a number of filtering techniques. The majority of these approaches, however, assume a standard underpinning data routing protocol that does not take into account the attack status or energy loss along the route. In terms of resistance to compromised node protection, each architecture offers almost equal resilience. The features of each design's energy usage, nevertheless, vary. We provide a fuzzy-based Optimal Secured Route (Fuzz_OSR) selection approach to save energy and prevent the formation of preferred paths. In order to prevent exploited intermediate filtering nodes getting involved in the verification process, new authentication keys are generated on a regular basis and supplied to the filtering nodes.
